heading: LOGOS-MODULE-CAPABILITY-AUTHORITY

heading: Abstract
text: Abstract

heading: Abstract
text: Every Capability Authority provider MUST be a local module provider backed by a local module instance.

heading: Abstract
text: The provider MAY use direct mode or local transport mode.

heading: Abstract
text: An implementation MAY co-locate or statically link Capability Authority code, but Runtime MUST still represent that code as a direct-mode local module instance.

heading: Abstract
text: Remote facades and host or deployment services that are not module providers MUST NOT be bound as Capability Authority providers.

heading: 1. Scope
text: 1. Scope

heading: 1. Scope
text: The provider MUST satisfy the LOGOS-MODULE-RUNTIME system-service binding checks before use and MUST NOT authorize its own initial binding.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: Every module-instance address named by this contract MUST resolve to one Runtime-known module instance.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: The Runtime engine, Runtime host, bootstrap machinery, operating-system objects, protected inputs, humans, and unauthenticated peers MUST NOT be represented as module instances.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: Runtime MUST supply Capability Authority with authenticated context for the consumer.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: 3. Authority Scopes

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: An allow decision MUST NOT broaden a requested scope and MAY narrow it.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: A decision based on a grant MUST NOT exceed that grant's current scope.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: For the Core scope shapes, required identity fields must be equal, and every constrained list in the narrower scope must be a subset of the broader scope.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: An optional identity absent from the broader scope is unconstrained; if it is present, the narrower scope must contain the same identity.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: If a broader provider-access scope contains `access`, a narrower scope MUST also contain `access` and narrow its method and event lists under the Runtime rules.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: Every permission definition MUST specify equivalent containment rules for its decoded `constraints` value.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: Every `actions`, `uses`, `scopes`, `providers`, `routes`, `modules`, `instances`, `modes`, `placements`, and `grant_ids` array that is present in a Capability Authority record MUST be non-empty unless its field definition explicitly permits an empty list.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: Every array whose elements are a set of scopes, actions, uses, providers, routes, modules, instances, modes, placements, method roots, event roots, or supporting grant identifiers MUST contain its elements in strictly ascending bytewise lexicographic order of each element's complete Logos deterministic-CBOR encoding.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: Such an array MUST NOT contain duplicate elements.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: A receiver MUST reject an unordered or duplicate set-valued array and MUST NOT silently sort or deduplicate a received, committed, or signed value.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: 3.1 Provider Access

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: Runtime MUST obtain this decision before satisfying an `all-runtime-visible` request or disclosing a provider's complete call surface through a module-selected call binding.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: For module-selected disclosure, Runtime MUST obtain one `discover` allow decision for the selected provider and each exact primary or interface contract in its validated call surface.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: If any contract view may not be disclosed, Runtime MUST fail the module-selected object request rather than omit that view or return a filtered surface.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: Method-level or event-level route access may narrow which operations the consumer may perform, but it MUST NOT produce a filtered construction input, disclose an unrelated contract, or change the selected contract identity.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: An implementation that needs a separately visible subset of a concrete contract MUST expose that subset as its own exact interface contract.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: For route creation or renewal, Runtime MUST include the allocated route identifier in the requested scope.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: It MUST also include the `access` requested for the route.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: For a call, publication, or subscription on an existing route, Runtime MUST include that route and an `access` value containing the one method or event declaration being checked.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: An allow decision used to keep a route or provider session usable MUST contain `valid_until`.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: Runtime MUST NOT keep the route or session usable after that time without a new allow decision.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: Runtime and the provider-side invocation boundary MUST reject calls, publications, subscriptions, and event deliveries outside the allowed scope.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: It MUST NOT be treated as a grant, an allow decision, or evidence that the consumer may invoke the declared operation.

heading: 3.2 Runtime Control

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: The scope applies to local `direct` and `local-transport` module execution and MUST NOT contain `remote-transport` in `modes`.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Direct execution MUST omit `placements`.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: `version` MUST NOT be present unless `package` is present.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: If `artifact` is present, `package` MUST also be present because the artifact identifier is package-scoped.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Outside the initial system-service bootstrap authorized under Section 1, Runtime MUST obtain an allow decision before asking Module Loader to realize a direct native implementation.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: The decision MUST cover the module execution operation and every required permission scope.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Runtime MAY allocate the module instance identifier used by the module consumer before loading code; allocation does not make the module loaded or ready.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Outside that initial bootstrap, Runtime MUST obtain an allow decision before asking Module Loader to realize a process, sandboxed process, or container.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: The decision MUST cover the module execution operation, selected hosted placement, and required permission scopes.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Runtime and the selected security profile MUST apply those constraints through their enforcement configuration; authority decisions and grants are not added to the Module Loader-owned realization descriptor.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Runtime MUST reject the operation if the selected execution path cannot enforce a required constraint.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Runtime MUST NOT claim containment against code that can access Runtime memory or unrestricted process resources.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: The `permission` field MUST unambiguously identify a specification or selected profile that defines the permission and its constraint schema.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

text: A profile that permits operating-system or platform access MUST define permission names and constraints for every facility it exposes. Relevant facilities include: … network connection, listening, protocol, destination, and port access;

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: A profile that permits operating-system or platform access MUST define permission names and constraints for every facility it exposes. Relevant facilities include: … process creation, signaling, and execution;

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: A profile that permits operating-system or platform access MUST define permission names and constraints for every facility it exposes. Relevant facilities include: … device, credential, secret, clipboard, notification, and UI integration access;

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: A profile that permits operating-system or platform access MUST define permission names and constraints for every facility it exposes. Relevant facilities include: … CPU, memory, process-count, file-descriptor, storage-growth, and similar resource limits;

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: A profile that permits operating-system or platform access MUST define permission names and constraints for every facility it exposes. Relevant facilities include: … placement, isolation, sandbox, and dangerous host or platform operations.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 4. Commitment Requirements

heading: 4. Commitment Requirements

heading: 4. Commitment Requirements

heading: 5. Decisions
5. Decisions
text: An allow decision MUST contain `allowed_scopes` and MUST NOT contain `denial`.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: A deny decision MUST contain `denial` and MUST NOT contain `allowed_scopes`, `valid_until`, `grant_ids`, or `commitment`.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: An allow decision MUST list every grant on which it depends.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Its `valid_until`, when present, MUST be later than `issued_at` and MUST NOT be later than the expiry of any expiring supporting grant.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Runtime MUST verify that the decision's consumer and requested scopes match its request.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Every allowed scope MUST be equal to or narrower than at least one requested scope.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: For every requested scope, an allow decision MUST contain at least one equal or narrower allowed scope.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Runtime MUST enforce every allowed scope and MUST verify that the attempted operation satisfies every narrowing introduced by those scopes.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Runtime MUST require a subject to satisfy at least one complete alternative and every narrowing shared by those alternatives.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Runtime MUST NOT combine selector fields from different alternatives to admit a subject that no individual alternative permits.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: An allow decision that omits coverage for a requested scope, broadens a requested scope, or contains an allowed scope that Runtime cannot enforce is malformed and MUST fail closed as an evaluation failure.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: If `valid_until` is absent, Runtime MUST NOT reuse the decision for another operation.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: If `valid_until` is present, Runtime may cache the decision only under the rules in Section 8 and MUST treat it as expired when the current time is greater than or equal to `valid_until`.

6. Grants And Revocation
text: Authority to invoke `issue_grant` does not itself permit the requested grant; active policy must allow the consumer to issue the requested scopes to that target.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: If it is present, it MUST be in the inclusive range from 1 through 1000.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Capability Authority MUST filter grants to those the authenticated consumer may inspect before applying the limit or creating a cursor.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: A cursor and result count MUST NOT reveal whether additional hidden grants exist.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: An issued grant MUST initially be `active`.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Its `expires_at`, when present, MUST be later than `issued_at` and later than the time at which the grant becomes active.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: An `active` grant MUST omit `revoked_at` and `revocation_reason`, and its `expires_at` MUST be absent or later than `now`.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: An `expired` grant MUST contain `expires_at`, MUST satisfy `now >= expires_at`, and MUST omit `revoked_at` and `revocation_reason`.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: A `revoked` grant MUST contain `revoked_at` that is not earlier than `issued_at`.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: It MAY contain `revocation_reason`.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: If a revoked grant has `expires_at`, `revoked_at` MUST be earlier than `expires_at`.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Capability Authority MUST treat a grant as expired at the expiry boundary even if persistence or event-publication work for the transition is still pending.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Grant administration methods MUST be available only through explicitly authorized provider access.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Capability Authority MUST use Runtime-supplied authenticated call context to determine who requested issuance, inspection, or revocation.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: It MUST NOT trust a policy-source or administrator identity supplied as an unverified method field.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

text: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: The corresponding `policy-change` audit record MUST use the same timestamp.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Capability Authority MUST verify against the committed transition that authorizations for every unlisted target remain valid for every consumer and enforcement context, including scope and commitment requirements.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Caller-supplied target information alone MUST NOT establish this guarantee.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: If completeness cannot be established, Capability Authority MUST omit the field.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: The set MAY be empty and MUST use the deterministic-CBOR ordering and uniqueness rules for set-valued arrays.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: The event MUST NOT expose targets the subscriber is not authorized to observe; filtering the set does not preserve its completeness guarantee.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MAY retain an existing execution authorization across the transition only when the authenticated event belongs to the same Authority binding, its previous revision matches that authorization's current policy revision, and its complete set excludes the exact execution target.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MUST then advance the retained authorization to the event's policy revision without extending its lifetime or scope.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Each retained authorization MUST account for every intervening policy transition; missing, inconsistent, or unverifiable transition information MUST end the authorization.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: A listed target's existing execution authorization MUST end.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Expiry, supporting-grant revocation or expiry, enforcement loss, and Authority-binding or notification-path loss MUST still end the authorization.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: A change to an unrelated grant does not by itself end an execution authorization; grant issuance MUST NOT widen or revive one.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: If the notification path is lost, Runtime MUST invalidate every cached decision from that Capability Authority.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST NOT perform another protected operation in reliance on an invalidated decision.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MAY retain allocated routes or sessions while obtaining a fresh decision, but they MUST remain unusable for protected operations until reauthorized.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MUST re-establish and confirm the grant and policy change notification path before a fresh evaluation may seed its decision cache.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST rebuild cache entries from fresh evaluations as protected operations require them and MUST NOT depend on reconstructing a snapshot of policy or grant state.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: If the re-established notification path is lost, Runtime MUST invalidate every newly cached decision again.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Capability Authority MUST emit `grant_changed` when a grant is issued, revoked, or becomes expired.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST emit `policy_changed` whenever active policy changes in a way that may affect an authority result.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Capability Authority MUST order each grant or policy state transition with its corresponding event.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: The new state MUST become active before the event can be observed, and the event MUST be committed to each applicable active Runtime notification path as part of that ordered transition.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: An evaluation ordered after the transition MUST observe the new state.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Event delivery MUST either succeed according to the subscription rules or cause Runtime to detect notification-path loss and invalidate all cached decisions.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: On `policy_changed`, Runtime MUST invalidate every cached decision from that Capability Authority.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: On grant revocation or expiry, Runtime MUST invalidate every cached decision that lists the changed grant.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Capability Authority and Runtime MUST deliver a change event only while the subscriber remains authorized for that event and the included grant or policy-change information.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: An event payload, subscription result, or diagnostic MUST NOT reveal a hidden grant.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: After a policy change, Runtime MUST re-evaluate dependent operations before performing another protected operation.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST make a dependent route unusable when the new decision denies the route or narrows its scope below the route's bound scope.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: After grant revocation or expiry, Runtime MUST prevent new dependent operations.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST terminate dependent provider sessions and subscriptions when their continued use would exceed current authority.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: When a required operating-system permission is revoked, its enforcement component MUST withdraw the permission or Runtime MUST stop the execution form.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: An implementation SHOULD cancel in-flight work when safe and supported.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: If cancellation is impossible, it MUST prevent follow-on operations and retain an audit record of the limitation.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Capability Authority MUST NOT directly mutate Runtime lifecycle, provider, route, Runtime Control, or transport-session state.

heading: 9. Audit Records
9. Audit Records
text: An `evaluate` failure record MAY contain the requested scopes only when they were successfully decoded and validated.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: A revocation failure MAY contain `target` only when the grant resolved and its target is known.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: Capability Authority MUST produce an audit record for each evaluation result or failure, grant issuance, grant revocation, grant expiry, and policy change.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: When an applied allow decision requires request or response retention for a call, the Runtime-controlled invocation boundary MUST produce a `call` audit record after the corresponding enforcement outcome.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: The record MUST contain the decision's `decision_id` and exact allowed call scope.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: Its `scopes` array MUST contain exactly one of these call scopes:

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: When an applied allow decision requires request or response retention for a call, the Runtime-controlled invocation boundary MUST produce a `call` audit record after the corresponding enforcement outcome. The record MUST contain the decision's `decision_id` and exact allowed call scope. Its `scopes` array MUST contain exactly one of these call scopes: … a `provider_access_scope` with the `call` action, one route, one selected provider, the selected contract, and one method declaration root; or

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: a `runtime_control_scope` naming the invoked Runtime and Runtime Control contract, with `methods` containing exactly one method declaration root and `events` absent. Every other present constraint MUST equal the constraint applied to the call.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: The record MUST contain the `request` or `response` commitment for each applicable `retain-root` requirement whose value was produced and successfully committed.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: If a required value was not produced or could not be committed, the record MUST use the `failure` outcome and MUST NOT claim a commitment for that value.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: A successful call record MUST contain non-empty `commitments`.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: A failed call record MAY omit `commitments` when no required value was successfully produced and committed.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: If a failed call record contains `commitments`, they MUST contain only successfully retained sides.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Every conforming Runtime MUST implement `logos.call-evidence.cose-sign1-ed25519` for call evidence.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text:
logos.capability_authority.call_evidence_profile =
    "logos.call-evidence.cose-sign1-ed25519"

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: logos.capability_authority.evidence_key_id = bstr .size (1..128)

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The container MUST be one tagged `COSE_Sign1` object using CBOR tag 18 from RFC 9052 and the fully specified `Ed25519` COSE algorithm `-19` from RFC 9864.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The protected header map MUST contain exactly `alg`, with COSE label `1` and value `-19`, and `kid`, with COSE label `4` and a `logos.capability_authority.evidence_key_id` value.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The unprotected header map MUST be empty.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The outer object and serialized protected header map MUST use the core deterministic encoding requirements of RFC 8949 Section 4.2.1.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The payload MUST be embedded as a byte string containing the exact deterministic-CBOR claim.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Protected trust input MUST map each accepted `kid` to exactly one producer Runtime identity and one exact 32-byte Ed25519 public key encoded according to RFC 8032.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: It MUST authorize that key specifically for call-evidence signing.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The same key material MUST NOT be used for package signing or TLS authentication.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Two accepted evidence keys MUST NOT use the same `kid`.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The Runtime host or its protected signing integration MUST keep the evidence-signing private key secret and protect it against unauthorized signing.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Evidence under an unknown or revoked `kid` MUST be rejected.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The signed `record` MUST satisfy every `call` audit-record rule in this section.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The `producer` MUST equal the Runtime identity authorized for the selected `kid` and MUST identify the Runtime whose controlled invocation boundary produced the record.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: If `proofs` is present, it MUST contain at least one request or response proof.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Each proof byte string MUST contain exactly one Logos deterministic-CBOR `verified-view` defined by LOGOS-MODULE-HASH-PROFILE.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Every proof MUST correspond to an existing commitment on the same side of the signed record.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: For each proof, the verified-view schema root, hash-profile identifier, hash-suite identifier, and commitment-model revision MUST equal the corresponding fields of the method's defining contract.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The verifier MUST determine that contract from the signed call scope's selected contract and single method declaration root according to Section 9.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Its schema subtree root and value root MUST equal the corresponding signed `audit_value_commitment`.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The verifier MUST then validate the complete verified view according to LOGOS-MODULE-HASH-PROFILE.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The verifier MUST reject a malformed or non-deterministic container or claim, an unknown or duplicate `kid`, an unaccepted header or algorithm, an invalid key or signature length, a failed signature, an incorrect profile identifier, an unauthorized producer, or any record or proof mismatch described above.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Before disclosing a container, the producer MUST apply the same audit authorization and visibility rules as `query_audit`.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Audit queries MUST require explicit authorization and MUST filter or redact information the authenticated consumer is not allowed to observe.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Audit records MUST NOT contain full route tickets, bearer credentials, private keys, or secrets.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Implementations MAY retain additional local audit detail, but the fields above define the common observation shape.

text: 10. Capability Authority Methods And Events

heading: 10. Capability Authority Methods And Events
text: Runtime MUST be authorized to invoke it through the bound system-service route.

heading: 10. Capability Authority Methods And Events
text: Ordinary consumers MUST NOT gain direct authority to call `evaluate` merely because they can request a provider route or invoke another Capability Authority method.

heading: 10. Capability Authority Methods And Events
text: Capability Authority MUST apply target and scope visibility before returning a grant.

heading: 10. Capability Authority Methods And Events
text: Capability Authority MUST return those fields unchanged or omit the grant.

heading: 11. Route And Credential Boundary
text: 11. Route And Credential Boundary

heading: 11. Route And Credential Boundary
text: They MUST NOT be presented by consumers as proof of authority and MUST NOT be accepted as bearer tokens.

heading: 11. Route And Credential Boundary
text: A protected transport profile MUST bind its route ticket or session credential to the consumer or authenticated session, selected provider, selected contract, and allowed method and event scope.

heading: 11. Route And Credential Boundary
text: It MUST also bind the target endpoint, Runtime route, authority decision, freshness, and revocation state.

heading: 11. Route And Credential Boundary
text: Missing, empty, invalid, expired, revoked, replayed, or incorrectly bound authorization material MUST produce no usable protected session and no ordinary module dispatch.

heading: 11. Route And Credential Boundary
text: Package-signature and call-evidence COSE objects MUST NOT be accepted as authorization material.

heading: 11. Route And Credential Boundary
text: Runtime MUST NOT place secret route tickets, private keys, or reusable bearer credentials in grant, decision, audit, Module Loader realization, package, or module lifecycle records.

heading: 13. Security And Privacy Requirements
text: 13. Security And Privacy Requirements

heading: 13. Security And Privacy Requirements
text: Runtime MUST treat an unavailable, malformed, mismatched, expired, or unverifiable decision as an evaluation failure and fail closed.

heading: 13. Security And Privacy Requirements
text: Runtime MUST validate every decision before enforcement and MUST NOT let a module bypass the decision path through a direct SDK, loader, Transport, or provider-host API.

heading: 13. Security And Privacy Requirements
text: Grant administration and audit observation MUST follow least privilege.

heading: 13. Security And Privacy Requirements
text: Implementations MUST minimize disclosure and apply the same authority checks to query results as to the underlying operations.

heading: 13. Security And Privacy Requirements
text: Full route tickets, proof-of-possession secrets, private keys, and reusable credentials MUST NOT be logged.

heading: 13. Security And Privacy Requirements
text: Diagnostic correlation SHOULD use non-secret decision, grant, route, and consumer references.
